points.description: Defines frame bursting: concatenating/sending multiple frames in one transmission (a burst) without releasing control of the channel, reducing overhead for small frames.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says multiple frames sent together, without keeping the channel or reducing overhead for small frames.

points.description: Gives one advantage over carrier extension: more efficient because frames are not padded with extension/garbage bits (less wasted bandwidth).
points.partial_credit: Half if says only 'more efficient' or 'less overhead' without linking to no padding.

points.description: Gives one disadvantage versus carrier extension: needs frames queued/buffered waiting to be sent, causing delay of frames.
points.partial_credit: Half if mentions complexity or delay vaguely without the need for waiting/buffered frames.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a correct definition, one advantage and one disadvantage relative to carrier extension. Give part marks for vague or half-stated parts; a general statement without the specific advantage or disadvantage earns about half of that point. Wrong statements lose only that point. Marks sum to 1 and may be given in quarter steps overall.
